From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightlinehealth.com>

Cc: ops@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live stream silence from Redwood endpoints — starting 09:05 PDT

Marissa / team,

We're seeing an increasing number of user-visible hangs on the realtime inference for our session-based workflow. Between 09:05 and 09:10 PDT today the response stream stopped emitting tokens for ~12-30s intermittently, then resumed. This is happening across multiple regions (us-west primary, and us-east fallback) and shows up as a series of chunked transfer closes in our client logs.

Sample client log snippet: 
- 2028-04-25T09:06:12Z GET /v1/stream -> 200
- 2028-04-25T09:06:17Z chunked-transfer-closed (client recovers)
- 2028-04-25T09:09:44Z websocket: read timeout (connection re-opened)

We're on Redwood hosted (api.redwood.ai) using model variant rwd-stream-1 (pinned). Error rate has spiked from <0.1% to ~3.8% over the last hour; latency p50 stable but p95 jumps to >8s during the stalls. This is impacting our demo today — can you triage? We have attached a trace and client captures.

Alex

Alex, Marissa —

Thanks for the report. We're seeing correlated anomalies in upstream edge metrics (increased HTTP/1.1 chunk frame gaps and abrupt connection half-close events) and a small cluster of model-variant workers reporting high kernel stalls around the same timestamps. Early hypotheses:

1) Intermittent proxy buffer congestion at the edge (NGINX timeout + chunk flush policy) causing chunked-transfer pauses;
2) KV cache pressure on the model worker triggering periodic GC on the runtime leading to token emission stalls;
3) A combination of client heartbeat thresholds + transient network jitter causing websocket clients to re-open and miss intermediate chunks (client-side recovery masks root cause).

I'm standing up a short war room (30 min) to gather traces — joining link below. Dev, can you confirm whether the affected workers were on any new kernel/quantized runtime deployed in the last 48 hours?

War room: https://console.redwood.ai/warrooms/WR-8062

— Sean

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live stream silence from Redwood endpoints — findings and temporary mitigations

Team / Alex —

We pulled traces for 09:00-09:30 PDT and correlating host logs. Findings:
- Edge (edge-*-nginx) showed spikes in sendfile queue lengths and chunk write stalls at 09:05:12 and 09:09:38 (matching Brightline traces). Upstream reported 504s for a handful of inflight requests that retried successfully.
- Two model workers in pool rwd-stream-1 were observed with long-tail GPU kernel stalls (~22-40s) while processing long-sequence sessions; these stalls coincide with token emission gaps.
- Connection-level TCP shows the socket remained established in most cases; the HTTP chunked stream stopped emitting bytes (i.e., silent stall rather than immediate reset).

Temporary mitigations applied at 11:10 PDT:
- Adjusted edge chunk flush interval to be more aggressive (flush smaller buffers sooner) to reduce sendfile queue buildup.
- Increased the model-worker soft time-slice to prevent GC/eviction from stalling token emission during heavy KV cache pressure.
- Enabled a 15s server-side heartbeat ping over websocket for the affected endpoint to surface silent stalls to clients faster.

Early results: error rate dropped from ~3.8% -> ~0.6% and observed token stream continuity improved in our canary traffic. We will monitor and iterate.

Action items:
- Engineering to instrument finer-grain per-token emission timing and add a guard to emit an empty chunk as a heartbeat if emission stalls >10s.
- SRE to run a full cap/burst test against rwd-stream-1 to reproduce GC-triggered stalls.
- CS/AM to coordinate a post-mortem and customer timeline.

I'll post fuller traces and the root-cause ticket (INF-9143) in the war room.

— Dev
Dev Patel

Subject: Re: Live stream silence from Redwood endpoints — post-incident summary and exec note

Alex —

Appreciate your patience while we dug in. High-level summary:
- Incident window: 2028-04-25T09:05:00-2028-04-25T12:55:00 PDT (primary anomaly cluster).
- Root cause (short): a confluence of edge chunk flush policy interacting with model-worker KV pressure which produced long-tail kernel stalls that paused token emission.
- Mitigations performed: edge flush tuning, worker time-slice tweaks, server-side heartbeat, and a client-visible temporary guard (emit empty chunk at >10s stall).

We've opened INF-9143 for tracking the long-term fixes (runtime scheduler changes, improved backpressure signalling, and a canary gating change for new runtime kernels). The full RCA + timeline is linked here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9143

As this did impact Brightline demo traffic and breached our p95 latency SLOs for the window, I've flagged this to leadership and recommend we offer a goodwill credit while our legal/finance team coordinates any formal SLA adjustments. Hannah (lead product) — can you propose the credit/recovery offer for review?

I'll schedule a 30-min post-mortem call with your ops team next week to walk through the technical details and planned fixes.

Best,
